summary: All four round-2 findings re-measured closed in my own tree: while->if dies only in legalPipeliningAtDepthTHREEIsPERMITTED; watermark keyed on 0L dies in aSUCCESSORChainAckingOutOfOrderIsCaught and TWOChainsAtDIFFERENTFloorsAreJudgedSeparately; base flattened to a global min dies in TWOChainsAtDIFFERENTFloorsAreJudgedSeparately; the message's + w replaced by the chain floor dies in theMessageNamesTheLOWESTUnconfirmedWriteNotTheFloor and aSUCCESSORChainAckingOutOfOrderIsCaught. Six further mutations of the round-1 watermark and round-2 per-epoch maps all die (base Math::min->max, confirmed set keyed on a constant, seen.contains(w+1) off-by-one, watermark.put dropped, watermark advance before seen.add, else-if->if). w < seq -> w <= seq survives but is semantically equivalent: the else-if is reached only when e.sequence() is in seen, and w is by construction the lowest sequence at or above the floor not in seen, so w != e.sequence(). This round's delta is tests and javadoc only, so there is no new production code to leave unconstrained. The documented floor hole is not blocking: its stated mitigation rests on checkChain arms that already carry tests (InvariantsTest.aHOLEInTheChainIsReported, InvariantsTest.anEntryBEYONDASealIsReportedAsI5), and M4.13's notes carry the CONTINUE-emission and run-both-checkers requirements. Full :sequencer:test green on the staged bytes.

findings.title: The own-write branch's report may name the wrong sequence and every test still passes
findings.failure_scenario: M4.13 feeds a failing seed's trace in and the sweep reports 'epoch 2 acked sequence 2 while its own write was unconfirmed' when the ack was actually of sequence 7. The violation is still counted, so the seed still fails; the engineer pinning it as a named regression test is sent to the wrong slot. This is the exact harm theMessageNamesTheLOWESTUnconfirmedWriteNotTheFloor was added this round to prevent on the other branch, and the symmetric branch is unpinned.
findings.surviving_mutation: In the first arm, replace `+ e.sequence() +` with `+ e.epoch() +` in the message: `new Violation("I5", "epoch " + e.epoch() + " acked sequence " + e.epoch() + " while its own write was unconfirmed")`. MEASURED in the reviewer tree: all 14 AckOrderTest tests pass. ackingAWriteThatWasNEVERConfirmedIsAVIOLATION asserts only invariant()=="I5"; ONECHAINSConfirmationsDoNotSatisfyANOTHERS asserts only detail contains "epoch 2", which the mutant still produces; anAckThatIsBothUnconfirmedAndOutOfOrderCountsONCE asserts only hasSize(1). No test asserts 'acked sequence <n>' on this arm.
findings.note: Non-blocking, and fixing it in a fourth round is probably the wrong trade -- the arm is round-1 code that already carries a verdict. A one-line assertion added when M4.13 first consumes the message would close it.
